cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Philippi, and he's just told them he counts everything as loss compared to knowing Christ Jesus (Philippians 1:1; 3:8). Now he stops to set the record straight: he hasn't already obtained all this, and he hasn't already been made perfect. Friend, if PAUL is still a work in progress, my blurry old stamps from the drawer days don't feel so bad.

cards.question: Paul hasn't been made perfect yet. So what does he say he does?

answers.text: He presses on to take hold of it
He waits for it to come to him
He rests on what he has done

cards.question: Paul presses on to take hold of that for which ___ took hold of him.

cards.text: Paul circles back to it: Brothers, he doesn't consider himself to have taken hold of it yet. But there's one thing he does, and he does it like a runner in a race.

cards.question: Paul's one thing works like a runner's. What does he say he's forgetting?

cards.text: So Paul forgets what's behind, strains toward what's ahead, and presses on toward the goal. I tried hopping forward while looking BACK over my shoulder once, friend, and me and the chocolate chips got real close, real fast.

cards.question: Paul presses on toward the goal to win the ___ of God's heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul widens it out beyond himself: "All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view."

cards.question: Paul says that if someone thinks differently about some issue, God will reveal this to them as well.
Some may still think differently. Nevertheless, what does Paul say we must do?

answers.text: Live up to what we have already attained
Keep quiet until everyone finally agrees
Stop and wait until more is revealed

cards.text: Now Paul points the Philippians to an example to follow. That's how you learn any new job, friend: shadow somebody, and PRAY it's not the guy who hits snooze six times and calls it a strategy.

cards.question: Paul tells the Philippians to join one another in following an example. Whose?
Paul tells the Philippians to watch only him and nobody else.

cards.text: Then Paul's voice gets heavy. He's told them this often before, and now he says it again, even with tears.

cards.question: Paul says many live as ___ of the cross of Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul describes them: "Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame."

cards.question: Paul says these people's minds are set on heavenly things.
Those people's minds are set on earthly things. But where does Paul say our citizenship is?

cards.text: And from heaven, Paul says, we eagerly await Someone. Not just wait, friend, EAGERLY await, like somebody with their nose on the front window every time a car slows down. Wrong car? Doesn't matter. Nose stays on the glass.

cards.question: From heaven, Paul says, we eagerly await a ___, the Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.text: This Savior has the power to subject all things to Himself, and with it He will transform our lowly bodies. Friend, I know a little something about being made new, and I'm telling you, it is GOOD.

cards.question: Jesus will transform our lowly bodies to be like His ___ body.

cards.text: Then Paul wraps it all up with a "Therefore," and look how he talks to them: "my brothers, whom I love and long for".

cards.question: Paul calls the Philippians his joy and crown.
Paul ends with a word to his beloved Philippians. What does he tell them they must do?

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences: "And from heaven, Paul says, we eagerly await Someone." / "Not just wait, friend, EAGERLY await, like somebody with their nose on the front window every time a car slows down." / "Wrong car?" / "Doesn't matter." / "Nose stays on the glass." It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The true or false statement "Paul tells the Philippians to watch only him and nobody else" can't be reasoned out. Nothing before it mentions anyone else to watch. Card 1 says only "an example to follow," and card 2 asks whose. The baker can only guess, or fall back on test-taking habits around words like "only." No story card ever tells the detail in 3:17 that they should carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern Paul set. The baker can leave Prep knowing only what Paul didn't say.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
